Sr NoRecommendations generated for   the management of plant parasitic nematodes and included in package of   practices
1
Soil solarization by 2-3 deep summer ploughings in the month of   May-June at 15 days interval followed by light irrigation and covering of   soil with 25 micron transparent polythene sheet for 30 days during June-July   for the management of root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.) in   Polyhouses.

2
Soil application of Trichoderma viride @   20g/m2, mixed with neem cake/FYM/Vermicompost @ 100g/m2 in the   beds for the management of root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.) in   tomato grown under polyhouse conditions

3
Management of root-knot nematode Meloidogyne   spp. in okra through soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5   kg/ha at the time of sowing

4
Management of root-knot nematode, Meloidogyne   spp. in tomato by using neem cake @ 750 g per m2 in nursery beds

5
For the management of rice root-knot nematode in rice   nursery, solarise the nursery beds before sowing for 15 days during summer.   Cover the nursery beds with transparent polythene sheet (25 µm thickness)   after light irrigation. Cover the edges of polythene sheet with soil to make   it air tight.

6
For the management of root-knot nematode in the   cucumber in polyhouse, take the following measures.
i) Remove and destroy the plants of the previous crop along with the   roots. 
ii) Solarise the soil during summer by covering it with a 25μm thick   transparent polythene sheet for 15-20 days, after light irrigation. Cover the   edges of polythene sheet with soil to make it air tight.
iii) Add FYM enriched with fungus (Purpureocillium   lilacinum) @ of 1 kg/m2 in the soil. For preparing enriched FYM, mix 2 kg   of fungus in 1 ton of FYM. Cover it with polythene sheet after sprinkling   with water. After 10-15 days, mix it well on the paved surface. 


Sr NoOutcome of the research and    accomplishments
1Pasteuria penetrans @ 1 x104  spores/g and Pseudomoans putida werefound promising in increasing plant height , fresh seedling weight of   brinjal seedling and reduced  root-knot   nematode multiplication.  Maximum and   significantly higher seedling height,(19.3 cm)   fresh seedling weight  (49.8 g)were observed in treatment where P.   putida was applied @ 1 lt. of culture broth   (2day old on NB  which was statistically at par to that P. penetrans @ 1 x104  spores/g soil. Minimum number of   galls (81.0) were also observed in P.   putida treatment while number of eggs per root system and final nematode   population were observed in  P. penetrans  @ 1 x104 spores/g soil as soil   application .
2A total of 90   soil samples collected from the rhizosphere of different crops were processed   for the detection of EPNs by insect bait method. EPNs were detected in 26   samples and were identified at generic level (Heterorhabditis and Steinernema)   based upon the colour of host cadaver. Out of 26 samples found infected with   EPNs, 19 were identified as Steinernema   spp and 7 were identified as Heterorhabditis   spp.  The total frequency of occurrence was   calculated to be 28.9%. Greater wax moth   (Galleria mellonella) is being maintained on artificial diet. 
3Four   modified media viz. Wout’s medium I,   Wout’s medium II, Dog biscuit medium and Modified dog biscuit medium were   used for in vitro culturing EPNs (Steinernema abbasi and   Heterorhabditis indica). Maximum and significantly higher multiplication   of Steinernema abbasi  was reported in in modified dog biscuit   medium. In case of Heterorhabditis indica maximum IJs were also   recovered in modified dog biscuit medium but there was much variation with   respect to the recovery of IJs among the media tested.
4Polyhouses of   five districts i.e.  Panipat, Sonipat,   Rohtak, Jhajhar and Fatehabad were surveyed during the month of March and   April, 2018 for the infestation of plant parasitic nematodes. Apart from the   survey, samples from the polyhouse growers received in the department were   also analysed for the infestation of nematodes.  A total of 122 soil and root samples from   different crops grown under polyhouse conditions were analyzed for nematode   infestation. Seventy out of 122 were found infested with root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne spp.) with a frequency of   occurrence 57.4%. The main crops in which infestation was recorded were   cucumber followed by tomato and capsicum. Lilium and Gerbera were found least   infected with root-knot nematodes. Population density of root-knot nematode   varied from 12-6450 J2/200cc soil.
4The rhizobactrial   strains were isolated from soil naturally infested with rice root-knot   nematode, Meloidogyne graminicola   by serial dilution method.  Bacteria   were also isolated from insects infected with entomopathogenic nematodes. Out   of twenty six bacterial strains tested (in   vitro) for nematicidal activities, five strains viz. Bacillus sp.; Pseudomonas   fluorescence; P. putida;   Providencia rettgeri; Vibrio sp. showed nematicidal properties in terms   of hatching inhibition and juvenile mortality at S/2 and S/4 concentrations.
5Screening   of 34 rootstocks against root knot nematodes in solanaceous vegetables and   cucurbits to vegetable grafting were done nematode infested conditions. RB2   and RB11 were found resistant/immune against root-knot nematode. No nematode   multiplication were observed in brinjal root stock RB6 and RB9.
6A total of 76,   soil and root samples were collected from rice growing areas of Jind, Bhiwani   and DSR fields of Fatehabad districts of Haryana. Out of these, 22 samples   were found infested with rice root-knot nematode (M. graminicola) with   28.94% frequency of occurrence. Fields of direct seeded rice were also   earmarked for monitoring the population build up in direct seeded rice was   also done. 23 soil and root samples were collected from the direct seeded   rice fields. Out of these eight samples were found infested with rice-root   knot nematode. The soil collected in the samples was used for the bioassay   for the detection of the nematodes. Other plant parasitic nematodes, which   were found, associated with the rice, belonged to genera Hirschmanniella,   Tylenchorhynchus etc. The population of other nematodes was below   pathogenic level. The weed flora of direct seeded rice is also being tested   for the host status of rice root-knot nematode
7The survey of   guava orchards was carried out in the month of April in Jind and Bhiwani   districts. Apart from the survey the guava root and soil samples received in the department   were also analysed for the infestation of plant parasitic nematodes. Among   all the plant parasitic nematode, root knot nematode, Meloidogyne spp.   was a major problem in guava orchards and nursery plants. In total, 121 soil   and root samples were analysed for root-knot nematodes. The major nematodes   reported were root-knot nematode and Helicotylenchus   spp. Out of 121 samples 92 samples, were found infested with root-knot   nematode with 76% frequency of occurrence. It was revealed from results that   root- knot nematodes, Meloidogyne spp.   had 80.0, 69.5 and 80.8 % frequency   of occurrence in Jind, Bhiwani and other samples, respectively. The population   density range was 49-829 J2/ 200 cc soil
8New   species i.e Steinernema   carpocapsae  and Heterorhabditis bacteriophora were used   for in vitro mass multiplication. Four modified media viz.  Wout’s medium I, Wout’s medium II,  dog biscuit medium  andmodified  dog  biscuitmedium  were  usedfor  in   vitro culturing.   Maximum and significantly higher multiplication of Steinernema abbasi and S.   carpocapsae (7244662 &   7793072 IJs respectively) was reported in   in modified dog biscuit medium.   In case of Heterorhabditis indica and H. bacteriophora maximum IJs (1532350   & 1648347) were also recovered in modified dog biscuit   medium but, there was much variation with respect to the recovery of IJs   among the media tested.
9Efficacy   of entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) in the management of insect-pests of   tomato was done under laboratory conditions. The virulence of Heterorhabditis indica was evaluated   against tomato fruit borer, Helicoverpa   armigera at four doses (5, 10, 20 and 40 IJs/insect larvae) under in vitro conditions. Results revealed   that H. indica was found to be   virulent against H. armigera and   could cause more than 50 per cent mortality at 10 IJs/larva underlaboratory conditions. The significant mortality in larvae started at   5IJs/insect larvae However, nearly 50 per cent mortality of the larvae was   observed at an inoculum level of 10IJs per larva after 48h (57.5%).
10Bio-management of root-knot nematodes, Meloidogyne   spp. in guava was done in infested orchard. The trial was conducted in   orchard naturally infested with root-knot nematode, at Village panniwala   Mota, Sirsa. The initial nematode population of root-knot nematode in the   soil was recorded to be 436, 484, 390, 445 and 429 J2 / 200 cc   soil in plots. Final nematode population of root-knot nematode was   significantly reduced in all the treatments as compared to untreated check.   Yield increased significantly neem cake enriched with Trichoderma viride @ 500 g/plant+neem cake enriched with Purpureocillium   lilacinum @ 500 g/plant as   compared to untreated check.
11Organic   management of Meloidogyne   spp.   infecting tomato in nursery was carried outin M.   incognita infested field.   Initial nematode population in the soil was 292 J2/200cc soil.  Organic amendments were applied ten days   before sowing of tomato nursery. Lowest root-knot index (2.0) was obtained in T5 where, neem cake @ 2 tons/ha   were applied followed by carbofuran 3G @ 2 kg a.i./ha as compared to untreated check (5.0). Minimum and significantly lowest   nematode population (120.7) was found in neem cake @ 2 tons/ha were   applied followed carbofuran 3G @ 2   kg a.i./ha. The maximum nematode population (331.2) and root-knot index (5.0) was recorded in untreated check
12Population of Meloidogyne graminicola multiplied on   all the host plant tested except on tomato and onion. Maximum multiplication   was observed in pearl millet (HHB67)   followed by rice. All the tested plants except onion and tomato were recorded   as hosts of Meloidogyne graminicola
13T. viride was most effective in   enhancing cucumber yield by 51.9 %, followed by P. lilacinus and P.   penetrans which enhanced cucumber yield by 37.0 and 22.2 %, respectively,   over untreated check. The reduction in nematode population in the soil was   more i.e. 32.8 % in T.viride treated beds followed by 21.5 and 14.3 %, respectively in P. lilacinus and P. penetrans treated beds over initial population. RKI was also   minimum (2.7) in case of T. viride   followed by P. lilacinus (4.0) over   untreated check (5.0)
14The Efficacy of EPN spray on   pests of cabbage  crops was evaluated   under field conditions. Spodoptera litura was observed feeding in   December, 2016 to January, 2017 in cabbage.Initial population was 2-4 larvae per plant.  Cabbage yield was significantly higher in   plots receiving two sprays of EPNs compared to Malathion 50 EC spray and   untreated control.
15Impact   of long-term) zero- tillage wheat trials at farmers’ fields in rice-wheat   cropping system was studied. Population of plant parasitic nematodes was less   in Zero tillage cropping system as compared to conventional tillage. The   possible reason is attributed to compactness of soil. Plant parasitic nematodes were lower under ZT-ZT than CT-CT and   similar trend was observed w.r.t. saprozoic nematodes. Yield of wheat and   pearl millet was higher under zero tillage than conventional tillage whereas   the yield of wheat and sorghum was higher under zero tillage than   conventional tillage.
16A total of 44 genotypes of rice were screened for   resistance against rice root-knot nematode during 2015, two genotypes, viz.,   AB1808 and AB1816 were found resistant to rice root-knot nematode. Rests of   the genotypes were categorized as moderately resistant, susceptible and   highly susceptible. Apart from the above 71 genotypes of rice were received from PC, AICRP   and screened for resistance against rice root- knot nematode.  Two genotypes viz., GP 9440 and IVT-2016-6 showed resistant reactions, eleven viz., GP7999, GP8212, GP8268, GP9281,   GP9501, GP9505, IVT-2016-1, IVT-2016-9, IVT-2016-27, IVT-2016-38 and   IVT-2016-43 showed moderately resistant reactions. Rest of the genotypes were   categorised as susceptible or highly susceptible

 nematode infested conditions. There   was 17.1 % yield loss in rice due to high population of  M.   graminicola at farmer’s field with a yield of 47.0 q/ha  in low infested field as compared to 39.0   q/ha in highly infested field. The estimated avoidable loss due to   application of cabofuran@3kg/ha was 11.4%..
18Management of rice root-knot   nematode, Meloidogyne graminicola   infesting rice was done and result revealed that Minimum no. of galls/20   seedlings (66), nematode population /200 cc soil (122 J2/200 cc   soil ) and root population (186 J2/200 cc soil) was observed T1   (Dazomet application @ 40 g/m2) which was statistically at par   with that of T2     (Soil solarization   of nursery bed with 25µm polythene sheet at least 15 days during April –May)   . All the treatments were significantly better from that of untreated check.   Maximum and significantly higher grain yield (5.2 t/ha) as compared to   untreated check (4.1 t/ha) was observed in treatment with Dazomet @ 40 g/m2   under polythene cover for 15 days before sowing

Recommendations generated for     field applications (2021-22)
For the     management of rice root-knot nematode in rice nursery, solarise the nursery     beds before sowing for 15 days during summer. Cover the nursery beds with     transparent polythene sheet (25 µm thickness) after light irrigation. Cover     the edges of polythene sheet with soil to make it air tight.
For the     management of root-knot nematode in the cucumber in polyhouse, take the     following measures.
  1. Remove and destroy the plants of the previous crop along with the     roots. 
  2. Solarise the soil during summer by covering it with a 25μm thick     transparent polythene sheet for 15-20 days, after light irrigation. Cover     the edges of polythene sheet with soil to make it air tight.
  3. Add FYM enriched with fungus (Purpureocillium     lilacinum) @ of 1 kg/m2 in the soil. For preparing enriched FYM, mix 2     kg of fungus in 1 ton of FYM. Cover it with polythene sheet after     sprinkling with water. After 10-15 days, mix it well on the paved surface.
